title: なるべく — as much as possible
summary: An adverb meaning “as much as possible, if at all possible.” It goes before a verb or adjective and shows that the speaker will try to do something, or asks someone else to try. It does not mean it will always be done.

patterns.form: なるべく＋動詞（依頼・努力）
patterns.gloss: なるべく早く返事をください: please do it as soon as possible

patterns.form: なるべく〜ようにする／ないほうがいい
patterns.gloss: I try to ～ / it is better not to ～ if possible

body.p: Put it before words of degree, as in なるべく早く or なるべく多く, to say you want to do it as far as possible. It goes well with requests (〜てください), efforts (〜ようにしている) and advice (〜ほうがいい).
The meaning is almost the same and they can be swapped. なるべく is common in everyday talk and sounds slightly softer, while できるだけ suggests a bit more effort and also suits formal situations.

examples.ja: なるべく早（はや）く返事（へんじ）をください。
examples.tr: Please reply as soon as possible.

examples.ja: 体（からだ）のために、なるべく歩（ある）くようにしている。
examples.romaji: Karada no tame ni, narubeku aruku yō ni shite iru.
examples.tr: For my health, I try to walk as much as possible.
examples.note: 〜ようにしている shows a habit of trying.

examples.ja: 甘（あま）い物（もの）は、なるべく食（た）べないほうがいい。
examples.romaji: Amai mono wa, narubeku tabenai hō ga ii.
examples.tr: It's better to eat as few sweets as possible.
examples.note: Used with advice: ～ないほうがいい.

pitfalls: It does not mean “definitely.” It means “as far as possible,” so use 必ず for things that must be done.
It is not normally used for completed past facts. Use it in requests, efforts and advice.
